title: Errors and result types — one screen
rememberThis: catch is unknown in strict TypeScript — anything can be thrown, unlike C# where only Exception types compile.
Result<T, E> for expected failures (validation, parse, not-found). throw for exceptional paths and programmer bugs.
Subclass Error for middleware mapping; discriminated unions for Result errors. Use cause to chain inner failures.
bullets: Never use as Error without instanceof — handlers crash while handling errors.
assertIsError and never in switch default give exhaustiveness when AppError unions grow.
catch (e: HttpError) does not filter at runtime — that is not C#. Narrow with instanceof inside unknown catch.
